description: World trap setup catalog: each row pairs a trap row ID and trap actor Blueprint asset name with the EGameTrapActionType behavior installed when AGameTrapManager::InitializeTrap initializes the spawned trap. It stores identity, asset selection and behavior selection, not trap statistics.

ID.simple: Trap row ID; it matches the DataTable row key.
ID.technical: FName value of FGameDataTableRow_Trap::Id (+0x08), serialized as ID while the export's ImportKeyField is Id; all 15 exported rows have ID equal to their row key. Callers normally look up by row key with Trap_FindTrapRow or a first-match FindRow over TrapDataTables (DTM +0x670). The shared finder rejects NAME_None only when bCheckNone=true, and every observed call to it passes false; the inlined CN_122 walk has no None test. The value is also read after spawn: FGameTrapAction_IceWall uses the cached trap row's Id to index C++ maps of rise effect, damage row and finish effect for TR_060_00/_10/_20 and TR_061_00/_10. Export IDs referenced by C++ include TR_010_00/_01/_02, TR_020_00, TR_030_00, TR_031_00/_10, TR_040_00/_10, TR_050_00, TR_060_00/_10/_20 and TR_061_00/_10. All exported IDs are populated; there is no None ID row.

FileName_BP.simple: Name of the trap actor Blueprint asset to spawn.
FileName_BP.technical: FName primary-asset name, not a filesystem path. SpawnTrap passes it to SpawnPooled, which forms FPrimaryAssetId(GamePrimaryAssetType_Trap, FileName_BP), resolves an already-loaded UClass through UAbramsAssetManager, and acquires or spawns an AGameTrap from the object pool keyed by that class; a missing class produces no trap. Config/DefaultGame.ini maps the Trap type to /Game/Traps with base class /Game/Traps/GameTrap_BP.GameTrap_BP_C. InitializeTrap caches the source row pointer on the spawned trap at +0x300, but only when both owner and row are non-null. The three exported TR_010_* rows intentionally share TR_010_00_BP while using three different ActionType values; TR_030_00 uses TR_032_00_BP, which is also the second trap asset in the CP_150 CharacterTrap preload array. Layout pin: row+0x10 is the spawn asset argument at retail 0x1414C2DE0.

ActionType.technical: uint8 EGameTrapActionType: 0 None, 1 VolcanoHoming, 2 VolcanoOneShot, 3 VolcanoTrigger, 4 FlowerMachineGun, 5 PlantRootMove, 6 PlantWall, 7 BodyRepel, 8 Uzumaki, 9 IceWall, 255 Invalid. The row constructor defaults this field to None; the export uses only the nine behavior values (IceWall x5, PlantWall x2, BodyRepel x2, and one each of the other six), with no None or Invalid row. InitializeTrap passes row+0x18 to SetTrapActionType. That function reuses the existing FGameTrapAction when GetActionType() matches; otherwise the switch installs the corresponding per-type action and initializes it with the controller's owner only when that owner is valid, then calls Start() if an action exists. None/Invalid or a case-less change leaves any existing action unchanged. CP_140 checks the cached row's ActionType to keep at most one VolcanoTrigger trap live; CP_150 checks it to replace the active FlowerMachineGun trap and reset shot state, and to special-case FlowerMachineGun/PlantWall trap-handle cleanup. SpawnFlag is a separate caller-supplied byte stored on AGameTrap, not part of this row field.

notes: Loader: GameDataTableManager.cpp:233 resolves the single 'TrapDataTable' loader into TrapDataTables (+0x670); the name is also registered at line 405. CharacterTrapDataTable (+0x4C0) is a separate per-character asset-preload table. BattleAsset_Traps appends CharacterTrap FileName_BP names directly as Trap primary assets; it does not join to TrapDataTable or read this table's ActionType.

Lookup precedence: every reader walks TrapDataTables in order and takes the first FindRow hit. Only one TrapDataTable is registered in this export/build. Missing rows or missing trap classes are handled by returning null before InitializeTrap in all observed spawn paths; InitializeTrap itself also null-guards owner/row.

Caches and aliases: the source row pointer is cached on AGameTrap at +0x300, the action object is cached in the action controller at +0x30 and reused when its type matches, and AGameTrap instances are pooled by loaded UClass. Caller-supplied SpawnFlag and CursedEnergyLevel are stored separately at trap +0x312/+0x314 and are not data-row fields.

Hard-coded data relationships: C++ callers and C++ maps key behavior on the row ID (for example TR_010_01/_02, TR_020_00, TR_030_00, TR_031_00/_10, TR_040_00/_10, TR_050_00, TR_060_00/_10/_20 and TR_061_00/_10), and IceWall maps TR_060_*/TR_061_* IDs to effects and damage rows. TR_030_00's asset name deliberately differs from its ID (TR_032_00_BP), and TR_010_00/_01/_02 share one Blueprint while differing in ActionType.

Export scope: one TrapDataTable with 15 rows, no shards or localization variants. The global CharacterTrap export has 5 rows, and each of the five per-character shards contains the matching single row. All 1,132 exported EffectDataTable rows have an empty Id_Trap_Background array, so the GameEffect trap-background path is code-verified but has no populated exported data example.

Placement is caller-controlled: SpawnTrap performs up to three overlap/ground-placement passes unless bSkipGroundPlace is true (CN_250 and the CP_150 homing-shot volley pass true; most other callers pass false). The table has no numeric timing, range or unit fields and no array indices of its own.

Evidence boundary: ActionType dispatch and consumer branches are traced in reconstructed C++ with decompiled RVAs. The current source also contains reconstructed FGameTrapAction_* implementations, but their verification states are mixed (MATCH, HOLD, DIFF and behavior-certified), so fine-grained effects are reconstructed behavior rather than byte-proven retail behavior. Retail Blueprint assets were not inspected; project guidance states Blueprints contain no logic, and no Blueprint-side evidence is claimed here.

usages.detail: Resolves the TrapDataTable loader into TrapDataTables (+0x670); TrapDataTable is also listed in the managed table-name set at line 405.
Trap_FindTrapRow walks the table array in order and returns the first FindRow hit; NAME_None is skipped only when bCheckNone=true, and observed trap callers pass false.

Action_SpawnTrapById performs the same first-match lookup, then spawns, initializes with flag 0 and hands the trap to the action owner's OnTrapSpawned; CP_150's TR_020_00 trail and CP_140's TR_010_01/_02 call this helper.
CP130_PlayTrackSequence selects TR_040_00 or TR_040_10 from bSpawnFlag and passes that flag to InitializeTrap.
An inlined first-match walk requests TR_050_00, then spawns and initializes it at an owner-relative offset derived from unique floats in row 7.
The homing-shot volley alternates TR_031_00/TR_031_10 by spawn index using another inline first-match walk; spawned traps receive the CursedEnergyLevel and are tracked in shot/played handles.
CursedEnergyAttack_1 requests TR_030_00, clamps the spawn range with unique floats and passes bAuto as the separate spawn flag.
The trap volley selects TR_060_00/_10/_20 by index and parity; line 2003 resolves TR_061_00/_10 from an 18-entry C++ spawn table of distance, angle and index values.

For each non-None EffectRow.Id_Trap_Background entry, the first table hit drives a component sweep and a trap spawn at the first matching background hit; exported EffectDataTable rows currently have empty arrays.
SpawnPooled converts FileName_BP into a Trap primary-asset ID and acquires or spawns the corresponding pooled AGameTrap; a missing class returns null.
SpawnTrap rejects a null row, spawns FileName_BP and optionally ground-places the trap with up to three passes.
InitializeTrap caches the row, sets owner and spawn flag, enables the collision keepers and forwards ActionType to SetTrapActionType; null owner or row clears the cached owner/row.
SetTrapActionType reuses a matching action or installs the per-type FGameTrapAction, initializes it when the owner is valid, then starts the valid action.
CP_140 inspects the cached row's ActionType to keep only the oldest VolcanoTrigger trap live, and removes that trap from its trigger list on finish.
CP_150 inspects the cached row's ActionType: FlowerMachineGun replaces ActiveTrap and releases TrapShot; line 1066 gives FlowerMachineGun and PlantWall special cleanup handling.
IceWall behavior reads the cached row's Id to look up rise effects, damage rows and finish effects.
Indirect asset-preload path: Character.Id_CharacterTrap resolves CharacterTrap rows, whose FileName_BP arrays are appended directly as Trap assets; TrapDataTable itself is not consulted here.
